findings: Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing. When enable_advanced_features=True and cursor.offset < 0, the code attempts queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset, which will raise AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.

Authorization check uses organization_context.member.has_global_access which may be overly permissive. A user with global access to an organization is not necessarily an administrator who should have access to advanced pagination features that bypass normal offset bounds.

The negative offset feature, if it worked, could allow users to manipulate cursor offsets to access audit log entries outside their intended pagination window, potentially exposing data they shouldn't see.
When cursor.is_prev is True, start_offset is set directly to offset without bounds checking, potentially allowing negative offsets to be passed to the queryset slice, which would fail.
Comment states 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' which is factually incorrect. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing.
The optimized_pagination query parameter is undocumented and creates a hidden API surface that changes pagination behavior, making the API inconsistent for consumers.
The new OptimizedCursorPaginator class has no corresponding tests to verify the negative offset handling, boundary conditions, or that the advanced features work correctly.

When `enable_advanced_features=True` and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code attempts `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`, which will raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.`

A user with global access to an organization is not necessarily an administrator who should have access to "advanced pagination features" that bypass normal offset bounds.
